title: My first game: a brick breaker in Godot. Free 5 level web demo.
author: gazotem
selftext:
Hey all! This is my first game, built with the help of AI. I'm a software engineer by trade with a lifelong passion for gaming, and AI finally let me act on it.

I had an absolute blast building it.

There are two modes:

* Amped: fast-paced, precision brick breaking
* Zen: the classic brick breaker experience

Play 5 levels free in your browser: [https://brickamp.com/play/game](https://brickamp.com/play/game)

I'm heading into prerelease in the next 1–2 weeks and would love more feedback before Early Access. Mobile versions are coming soon too.

Steam page: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5211360/BrickAmp/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5211360/BrickAmp/)

Happy to answer any questions about the process!

**Tools**

* Claude Code did most of the work (Cursor early on)
* Godot 4.6 as the engine, with a Godot MCP plugin so the AI can inspect the running editor and game
* Suno for music
* Linear for bugs and ideas: I dictate voice notes and an AI skill files them as issues
* Git worktrees so several AI sessions can work on different features in parallel (20+ at once at times)

**I switched Engines**

BrickAmp started in TypeScript + PixiJS in the browser. In March 2026 I ported the whole thing to Godot 4: game logic, procedural rendering, 26 themes, levels, power-ups, HUD and audio. I moved for native builds (Steam Deck, Mac, iOS), performance, and a real scene and shader pipeline. Godot's web export also gives me the browser demo for free.

**The TUI (Ill post screenshot in comment)**

To keep up with a dozen AI sessions, I built a terminal control panel called brun (Python + curses). It lists every worktree with its git status, PR and CI state, and what its Claude session is doing (working, needs input, failed), plus model and token spend. One keypress launches that branch's build of the game, tails its logs, takes a screenshot, makes a web build, or deploys to my Steam Deck over SSH. When an agent gets stuck waiting on me, I get a desktop notification. It's basically mission control for running a team of AIs.
